svg.aria-label: The story of PDF Distiller: a new lecture slide notification arrives on your laptop; scrolling reveals headers, logos, and visuals made for a university lecture hall screen rather than paper. Hesitating at Print, you open PDF Distiller locally via Spotlight and drop the slides in. You explicitly click to remove the decorative mountain photo first, then select Remove from all pages on the repeated pink and yellow banners while leaving the engineering chart untouched. Saved ink dissolves into halftone dots returning to your cartridge, wallet, and nature, leaving crisp paper for calm study. Print the slides, not the ink.

g.text: New lecture slides arrived. Let's open them.
Great slides—full of headers, logos, and large visuals.
Designed for the lecture hall screen—not for paper.
I focus better on paper—but why waste ink on notes I'll read once?
Open PDF Distiller locally. Drop the slides in.
Remove the photo and repeated banners. Leave the chart untouched.
Crisp paper. Clear mind. Less waste.
Print the slides, not the ink.
